title: Smt. Reeta Mishra v. State of U.P. and others
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Saumitra Dayal Singh, J.; Indrajeet Shukla, J.
disposition: Writ disposed of; remanded to Assessing Officer under Clause 6.8 subject to deposit of Rs. 35,000.
headnote: Where compliance with assessment procedure is unclear and the consumer alleges no hearing before creation of an electricity demand, the High Court may dispose of the writ by directing, subject to a part-deposit, that the Assessing Officer decide the objection under Clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 by a reasoned order after personal hearing and confrontation with adverse material.
facts: Smt. Reeta Mishra challenged a recovery citation dated 22 July 2025 seeking to recover Rs. 1,52,145 towards electricity dues. She alleged that no opportunity of hearing was given before the demand was created. The Court noted that it was not clear whether the assessment procedure had been fully complied with, and saw no useful purpose in keeping the petition pending or calling for a counter affidavit.

holding_units.holding: Where it is unclear whether assessment procedure was fully complied with and the consumer claims no hearing before the demand, the writ may be disposed of directing that, subject to depositing Rs. 35,000 towards the disputed demand within one month and applying to the Assessing Officer within a further week, that officer shall decide the objection by a reasoned speaking order under Clause 6.8 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, after confronting the consumer with all adverse material and granting personal hearing, preferably within two months.

not_decided.point: Whether assessment procedure was fully complied with and whether the recovery of Rs. 1,52,145 is sustainable on merits
not_decided.note: Compliance was recorded as unclear; the demand was remitted without a merits decision.
